question: Derive the Z-transform of a causal exponential signal x[n] = a^n * u[n].
_instructions: For each step set 'human_correct' to true/false. Set 'error_type' to one of: algebra, sign, missing_term, substitution, definition, none. Set '_filled' to true when done. Set 'final_answer_correct' to true/false after comparing 'generated_final' to 'expected_final'.

steps.description: Start with the definition of the Z-transform
Substitute x[n] = a^n * u[n] into the transform
steps.notes: Direct substitution of x[n] = a^n * u[n]. Correct.

steps.description: Use the fact that u[n] is zero for n < 0 to change summation limits
steps.notes: u[n]=1 for n>=0 and 0 otherwise, so lower limit correctly changes to 0 and u_n drops out.

steps.description: Combine terms into a single geometric sequence
Recognize this as an infinite geometric series
steps.notes: Correct identification with r = a*z^(-1) = a/z. Convergence requires |r| < 1, i.e. |z| > |a|.

steps.description: Apply the formula for the sum of an infinite geometric series when |r| < 1
Multiply numerator and denominator by z to simplify
steps.notes: Multiplying numerator and denominator by z: z / (z - a). Matches expected final answer.
